chat.answer:
Based on my analysis, Santiago is a final-year Computer Engineering student at the University of La Rioja, specialising in knowledge management, and he wants to work in applied AI: language models and computer vision. He is currently an intern at Encore Lab, where he is building, on his own, a cloud portal for the clients of a grant consultancy, which is also his bachelor's thesis.

He measures a model against others before choosing it. He compared five CNN architectures to classify satellite images and pitted DistilBERT against ULMFiT to classify prompts. In his face search he timed the VP-tree index against a linear search, and when the index came out slower, he documented it.

He grew up in Quito, went to a French school and now lives in Spain, so he adapts quickly and works comfortably in Spanish, English and French.

items.title: Full-stack developer intern
items.text: I am the sole developer of a cloud portal for the clients of a grant consultancy, working under my managers' supervision; it is also my bachelor's thesis. I built the synchronisation end to end. In the consultancy's legacy internal system (PHP and MySQL), I capture each change in the same transaction as the operation and send it every 5 minutes over HTTPS, one way and with retries, so the internal network is never exposed. On the portal side, a NestJS API on PostgreSQL receives the data, and documents of up to 512 MiB go through quarantine and an antivirus scan before they become available. I also designed and built the portal's infrastructure with Docker (containers, volumes, PostgreSQL, backups and antivirus) and secured the sync API: every request is verified and strictly validated against the contract. The next phases will add users with access to several companies, document requests, tracking of financial returns and LLM features.
items.stack: TypeScript · NestJS · Angular · PostgreSQL · TypeORM · zod · PHP · MySQL · Docker · ClamAV · Claude Code

items.title: Full-stack developer (freelance)
items.text: I am building the website of an Ecuadorian travel agency that mostly sells trips to the Galápagos. Both parts are still in development: the frontend, bilingual and in Next.js, and the backend in FastAPI and PostgreSQL, which already has tests. For now a static version is published. GitHub Actions deploys it automatically, and the final product will run on a dedicated server and be deployed with Docker, with frontend and backend connected.

cv.summary: Final-year Computer Engineering student at the University of La Rioja. I want to work in applied AI, on language models and computer vision. I have trained, evaluated and served models with Python, scikit-learn and PyTorch. At Encore Lab I am the sole developer of a cloud portal for the clients of a grant consultancy, which is also my bachelor's thesis. Available from June 2027.

bullets: Built the sync mechanism between a consultancy's legacy system (PHP, MySQL) and a cloud portal (NestJS, PostgreSQL): transactional change capture and one-way delivery over HTTPS, following an internal communication protocol, without exposing the consultancy's internal network.

Designed and implemented the portal's infrastructure with Docker (containers, volumes, PostgreSQL, backups and ClamAV antivirus) and the security of the sync API: verification of every request, strict contract validation and document quarantine.
Building the bilingual website (Next.js) and the backend (FastAPI, PostgreSQL, with tests) of an Ecuadorian travel agency focused on the Galápagos.
Built a face search over 21,678 press photos: detection with dlib's CNN, FaceNet embeddings and a VP-tree index of 38,299 faces.
Calibrated the similarity threshold with a ROC curve and an F1 sweep to an F1 of 0.911. Compared the VP-tree index with a linear NumPy search, which at this scale was 8 to 11 times faster.
Fine-tuned a ResNet18 with fastai to classify satellite images into 4 classes: 99.82% test accuracy.
Compared five CNN architectures (ResNet18 and 34, EfficientNet-B0, MobileNetV3 Small and ConvNeXt Tiny) under the same conditions.
Classified LLM prompts into 10 topics with a fine-tuned DistilBERT: 67.35% accuracy and a weighted F1 of 0.667 on a 1,550-prompt test set.
